## ✨ Highlights

The last two findings of the 2026-11-05 security review - the two that
needed a decision - and a dependency fix.

- 🔐 **A node's identity now takes the fleet's recovery kit**: replacing a
  node *with* its CA needs a certificate the fleet's root signs (`-kit`)
  or the node's own. An everyday 12-hour admin certificate still exports
  the rest of the state - and the documentation now says plainly what an
  admin certificate is worth.
- 🙈 **The Controller hides rescue and pairing codes** in the machine
  consoles it shows its operators.
- 📦 **klauspost/compress 1.20.2**, the zstd decoder's fix.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Replacing a node with `-identity`** takes `-kit KIT` - the fleet's
  recovery kit, opened on your machine for that one call - on
  `janusctl system state export` and `janusctl system state import
  -from`, or the node's own credential (`janusctl access rescue`).
  Without `-identity`, nothing changes; a cluster made from a node never
  carried the identity
  ([replacing a node](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/replacing-a-node.md#identity-the-same-node-or-a-new-one)).
- **A rescue code is read on the hypervisor's own console** - its screen,
  or its serial console while nobody watches it from the Controller: the
  Controller's console of a machine hides it now
  ([recovery](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/recovery.md#neither)).

## 🔒 Security

- **Janus itself** (nodes), its own code:
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-031](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.07/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-031.json) - A short-lived fleet admin certificate could carry a node's CA key away. On a node that trusts a fleet, any admin certificate - a Controller sign-in's, an API token's, `janusctl fleet`'s - could export the node's identity, a key good for years: the identity now goes only to a certificate of the node's own CA or of the fleet's root itself.
- **Janus Controller itself** (the Controller), its own code:
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-032](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.07/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-032.json) - The Controller relayed a machine's rescue code to the machine's operators. An operator watching a machine's console while an admin rescued it could use the code - an hour's admin certificate of the node - first.
- **github.com/klauspost/compress (Go module) v1.20.1 → v1.20.2** (nodes):
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-116591](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GO-2026-6865) - Panic on two-block frames in github.com/klauspost/compress. On a node the zstd decoder only reads the node's own LOGS partition and squashfs images (an update bundle an admin gave it): no path for a stranger; a panic would restart janusd, not HAProxy.

## 🔌 The node API

- `SystemService.StateExport` and `StateExportGrant`: `include_identity`
  only for a certificate signed by the node's own CA or by the fleet's
  root itself - an issuing CA's certificate gets `PermissionDenied`.

## 🧰 Nodes

- **The identity is apart from the rest of the state**
  ([JANUS-2026-031](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.07/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-031.json)):
  the node's CA key leaves it only for a rescue certificate, an older
  node's admin credential or a certificate the fleet's root signs. Its
  certificates' keys, its ACME account and its TLS ticket keys still go
  to an admin calling the node itself - the documentation now says so
  ([trust](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/internals/trust.md#what-a-node-accepts)).

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Rescue and pairing codes hidden in a machine's console**
  ([JANUS-2026-032](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.07/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-032.json)),
  for every reader, admins included - as the private keys already were.

## 🔧 janusctl

- **`-kit KIT`** on `system state export` and `system state import
  -from`: janusctl opens the kit (its passphrase asked, or
  `JANUS_KIT_PASSPHRASE`), signs a one-hour certificate with the fleet's
  root for that call alone, and keeps neither.
